kai: ran a 10-min nsys trace on canary after we bumped continuous_batch_window -> 48ms. seeing a recurring queue-tail spike ~30-40ms that wasn't there at 24ms. attaching short timeline dump below.
maria: ugh. is the spike purely queue time or compute backpressure? any kernel switch around the window boundary?
kai: looks like queue time. nsys shows long gaps between enqueue and kernel start. NVTX regions show 'dispatch' -> then 30ms idle -> 'matmul_int8_fused' starts. interestingly, kernel selection flips between two matmul variants mid-run.
aj: could be kernel affinity heuristic picking a higher-throughput kernel that needs more warmup/wavefronts and thus longer launch latency for small batches.
linda: do we still have the kernel-selection fallback TTL? maybe the runtime keeps using a variant because avg latency looked better historically.
kai: i dumped the kernel-choice log. snippet:

```
[2026-02-15T14:12:03Z] batch_size=5 seq_len=128 -> chosen_kernel=matmul_f32_256x32
[2026-02-15T14:12:03Z] batch_size=6 seq_len=64  -> chosen_kernel=matmul_int8_wmma (latency_est=12.4ms)
[2026-02-15T14:12:03Z] batch_size=7 seq_len=128 -> chosen_kernel=matmul_int8_wmma (latency_est=10.2ms)
[2026-02-15T14:12:03Z] batch_size=4 seq_len=256 -> chosen_kernel=matmul_f32_256x32
```
kai: the int8_wmma kernel has higher theoretical throughput, but in practice for these micro-batches it has an expensive kernel-launch/occupancy handshake causing the 20-40ms gap when it schedules. at 24ms window we rarely formed batches large enough to trigger the heuristic; at 48ms the window pushes more requests into that size/shape combo so the heuristic flips.
perf-bot: CPU-side stack shows heavy host-side serialization when kernel selection code path executes (lock on kernel cache). 1200 samples -> top frames: runtime::choose_kernel(), kernel_cache::get_or_create(), cudaLaunchKernel.
aj: two interacting issues then: (1) kernel-selection heuristic is too eager based on throughput proxy; (2) continuous batching window changes distribution so more batches hit the pathological path. plus possible KV-cache prefetch thrash?
kai: yes, KV-cache sweeps show higher prefetch churn. When the batch window increases we see more prefix-KV cache refills because requests coming as larger batches touch different token offsets. I have a perfetto link: https://perfetto.example/runs/1976543210/timeline
maria: can you try forcing kernel affinity (prefer f32) for a test run to confirm? also test disabling KV prefetch for 10s.
kai: did a quick A/B: forced kernel policy -> gap disappears, median latency drops 22%. disabling KV prefetch -> small further improvement (~6%) but increases model token compute due to more cache misses later.
ops: what's the short-term mitigation? roll back batch window to 32ms? or short-circuit kernel selection for small batches?
linda: we have a config flag runtime.kernel_selection.threshold_batch_size. set it to 8 to avoid switching for micro-batches. that combined with reducing continuous_batch_window to 36ms should be safe.
aj: long-term we should update the cost model: incorporate launch-overhead penalty and host-side locking cost into the kernel selection estimator. and add a 'cold-start' penalty for kernels that involve additional workspace allocation.
kai: next steps I pushed a canary patch: (1) add launch_overhead estimate to kernel profiles (2) heuristic: prefer lower-launch-overhead kernel when estimated batch_latency < 20ms (3) KV prefetch backoff during initial ramp. canary diff: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/+/r1234
maria: nice. schedule a 1-hour perf test with nsys + perfetto and collect host stacks. leave the canary on for 30m then revert to baseline for comparison.
ops: I'll schedule on canary pool agora-rw-3 between 2000-2100 UTC. tagging @perf-bot to collect traces.
perf-bot: scheduled run queued. will post artifacts to the trace bucket when done.
kai: tl;dr: bumping continuous_batch_window exposed a kernel-selection/cold-launch regression + amplified KV prefetch churn. mitigation = tightened selection thresholds + smaller batch window + KV prefetch backoff. long-term = update cost model to include launch/lock overheads and add pre-warm warmup for int8 kernels.
notes: thread is a short troubleshooting convo with a canary + perf-bot. contains command snippets and a perfetto link. no title field included per agents.md rules.
